Official myTax 2026 WHM instructions (ranks for the head term): who completes the section, what WHM net income is, and the nationality rule for WHMs who are Australian residents for tax purposes.

changes.new_text:
Eyebrow: Key figures
H2: Working holiday tax return key figures for 2025-26
Table caption: The figures a 417 or 462 tax return turns on. Checked against ato.gov.au and servicesaustralia.gov.au, November 2026.
Columns: What | Figure | Source
Row 1: Financial year a return covers | 1 July to 30 June. Each year is its own return. | ATO
Row 2: Working holiday maker tax rates (2025-26, unchanged from 1 July 2026) | 15% up to $45,000, 30% from $45,001 to $135,000, 37% from $135,001 to $190,000, 45% above $190,000. No tax-free threshold. | ATO
Row 3: Withholding with no TFN on file | 45% | ATO
Row 4: Medicare levy | 2% of taxable income. An exemption needs a Medicare Entitlement Statement. | ATO, Services Australia
Row 5: Deadline if you lodge yourself | 31 October after the year ends. For 2025-26 that was 31 October 2026, which has passed. A late return can still be lodged. | ATO
Row 6: Where a refund is paid | Only into a financial institution account located in Australia. | ATO
Row 7: Lodging early, before leaving Australia permanently | Paper return only. The ATO says early lodgements take 50 business days to process. | ATO
Row 8: Processing of returns lodged online | The ATO says most process within 10 business days. Any refund usually reaches your account about 14 business days after lodgement. | ATO
changes.why: No competitor has a correct, dated, sourced figures block (peakifi's rates table carries a 32.5% band that no longer exists). A compact sourced table is the passage AI answers and featured snippets lift for 'working holiday tax return' and 'backpacker tax rate'. Rows 6 to 8 are facts no top-5 page states. All figures are from llms.txt Key facts or ATO pages fetched today.

changes.where: src/app/(site)/tax-return/page.tsx FAQS item 'Can I lodge my tax return before I leave Australia?' (answer starts 'Only in one situation.')
changes.new_text:
Only in one situation. If you are leaving Australia permanently before 30 June and will not earn any more Australian income that year, other than interest, dividends or royalties, the ATO accepts an early return before the year ends. An early return has to be lodged on paper, and the ATO says early lodgements take 50 business days to process.

If you leave without lodging, nothing is lost: the return can be lodged online after 30 June, from wherever you are, and is usually processed much faster.
changes.why: The current answer omits the ATO's paper-only rule and the 50 business day processing time (ato.gov.au 'Lodge your tax return before leaving Australia'). Without it the page implies an early return follows the same fast online path as the 7 steps, which is wrong. This is also the only FAQ here that maps to a query the ATO page itself ranks for, so accuracy is what earns the citation.

changes.where: src/app/(site)/tax-return/page.tsx FAQS, insert after 'When is a working holiday tax return due?'
changes.new_text:
Q: Which financial year does my tax return cover?
A: The Australian financial year runs from 1 July to 30 June, and each one needs its own return. If you worked from March 2025 to February 2026, that is two returns: 2024-25 for March to June 2025, and 2025-26 for July 2025 to February 2026.
changes.why: A stay that crosses 30 June is the norm on a working holiday, and pvtistes ranks with exactly this worked example. A short self-contained answer is quotable and explains why we 'work through them oldest first'. FAQPage schema picks it up automatically from FAQS.

changes.where: src/app/(site)/tax-return/page.tsx FAQS, insert after 'Can my return be lodged after I have already left Australia?'
changes.new_text:
Q: What if my employer was not registered for working holiday makers?
A: The 15% rate depends on the employer being registered with the ATO as an employer of working holiday makers. If yours was not, tax was withheld at the foreign resident rate, which starts at 30 cents in the dollar. Your return is assessed at the working holiday maker rates, so the difference is settled when it is lodged.
changes.why: peakifi carries this as an FAQ and a full H2; on our page the fact is only in a card, which is not in FAQPage. Every fact is already on the page (REFUND_SOURCES card 3).

facts.fact: Working holiday maker rates: 15% to $45,000, 30% $45,001 to $135,000, 37% $135,001 to $190,000, 45% above $190,000; unchanged from 2025-26 into 1 July 2026; no tax-free threshold.
Withholding with no TFN on file: 45%.
Medicare levy 2% of taxable income; exemption via a Medicare Entitlement Statement for non-RHCA countries.
Self-lodger deadline 31 October after the year ends; 31 October 2026 for 2025-26, passed; late returns can still be lodged.

Early lodgement only if leaving Australia permanently before 30 June and no further Australian-sourced income other than interest, dividends and royalties; must use the paper form; 'Processing for early lodgments is 50 business days.'
'You can lodge your tax return online from your home country.' Early return when leaving permanently 'must' be paper and 'takes longer to process'.
'We'll only pay tax refunds into recognised financial institution accounts located in Australia.'
'Most returns lodged online process within 10 business days.'

2025-26 WHM section applies to income earned on a 417 or 462 visa between 1 July 2025 and 30 June 2026. WHMs who are Australian residents for tax purposes and nationals of Chile, Finland, Germany, Israel, Japan, Norway, Turkey or the United Kingdom pay resident rates; nationals of other countries pay WHM rates.
Unregistered WHM employer withholds at the foreign resident rate starting at 30 cents in the dollar; refunds usually about 14 business days after lodgement (site's own approved wording).
